newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan auto exports up for first time in five years.
newsitem.headline: Japan auto exports up for first time in five years.

text.p: Japan's vehicle exports rose for the first time in five years in the 1996/97 fiscal year, helped mainly by the weaker yen, an industry body said on Monday.
Exports rose 6.2 percent from a year earlier to 3,847,865 vehicles in the year to March 31, the first increase in five years, the Japan Automobile Manufacturers' Association said.
But the value of all car and car part exports, however, fell 1.2 percent from a year earlier to $78.34 billion as a result of higher local procurement of car parts.
The export gains were fuelled by the weaker yen, which boosted shipments, an association official said.
Exports to the United States rose 5.3 percent from the year earlier period to 1.17 million vehicles in 1996/97. They had fallen in the previous year.
Exports to the European Union rose for the first time in six years, up three percent to 818,008 vehicles, while exports to Asia fell four percent to 606,415, the association said.
"But we expect overall exports in 1997/98 to remain flat against last year because of an anticipated shrinkage in the U.S. market later this year," the association official said.

"We estimate exports of 4.06 million units in 1997/98 if the average yen/dollar rate is about 120 yen. The increase is based on sales of light sport-utility vehicles which are not produced in the United States," Nikko Research senior analyst Noriyuki Matsushima said.

Exports are expected to increase not only to the United States but to other areas, including the Middle East and Europe, in view of the weak yen which makes Japanese cars more competitive in international markets, Matsushima said.

Matsushima said rising Japanese car exports are unlikely to be the key trade issue with the United States for the time being because sales and profits of the three big U.S. automakers are in good shape due to the buoyant economy there.
But U.S. manufacturers, especially the "Big Three", have complained that they are being hurt by the weaker yen, which makes Japanese goods cheaper in global markets.
